definition: commission and omission parting only at the consent multiplier, never at attribution

settled:
Causal attribution is blind to the category. It scores the actual marginal contribution, not whether it was a direct act, an indirect one, or a failure to act. Direct beats indirect beats omission is a rule of thumb about typical causal weight, and I use the real weight. A lone agent who could have prevented a harm and did not is attributed as a direct act of the same size.

The distinction enters at one place only, the consent multiplier. Committing a harm is charged the share and then consent-weighted. Failing to prevent one is charged the share bare.

Both shares dilute when many agents contribute. Only commission also carries the multiplier, which for a severe harm grows steeply as consent falls and swamps any finite dilution. No mob is large enough to make a non-consensual killing cheap per head.

Omission is finite, capped at the harm itself, so a big enough crowd of co-omitters can drive it small per head. That is why negative duties come out stricter than positive ones.

title: Where Doing And Failing To Do Differ
